newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian flagship aground off rebel Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Italian flagship aground off rebel Albanian port.

text.p: Italy's flagship in a multinational security force ran aground in high winds off the rebel-held Albanian port city of Vlore on Tuesday, a military spokesman said.
"The Vittorio Veneto got stuck in stormy seas," Lieutenant Colonel Gianfranco Scalas, spokesman for the eight-nation mission to Albania, told Reuters.

The Vittorio Veneto, a cruiser and helicopter carrier, is the flagship of the Italian-led mission, which aims to protect aid deliveries to the poor after an armed insurrection triggered by failed investment schemes.
"The ship is stuck about 500 metres (yards) from the shore in misty, rainy conditions and choppy seas," Petrit Ago, a former Albanian navy commander and a local resident, told Reuters.
Two tugs and three Italian navy vessels hovered near the Vittorio Veneto, which towered over them.
"I think the Italians have a difficult problem to solve here," Ago said. "The two little tugs aren't going to be very effective in towing this huge ship."

The Italian navy said in a statement in Rome: "The Vittorio Veneto drifted during buffeting from a strong sirocco wind because the anchor did not hold, and the stern came to rest on the sandy and muddy sea bottom. There is no visible damage to the ship or to people."
It added that the navy was moving suitable boats to the area for the rescue operation and that the Vittorio Veneto was still carrying out its command and control duties.

The Vittorio Veneto belongs to a U.N.-backed security mission to protect humanitarian aid deliveries in the anarchic Balkan state. Some 160 Italian troops disembarked from Italian navy ships off Vlore on Monday.

Vlore is controlled by a rebel committee, which rejects the authority of President Sali Berisha whom it blames for the collapse of fraudulent savings schemes in which many Albanians had invested their life savings. At least 300 people have been killed in the violence in Albania.

The United Nations' World Food Programme (WFP) sent 220 tonnes of wheat flour from the western port of Durres to 4,430 destitute families in Elbasan, an industrial town 50 km (30 miles) southeast of Tirana, WFP officials said.
State social security payments to the poor have dried up since the insurrection broke out in late February.

Witnesses said Italian soldiers from the multinational mission had secured the roads but did not provide an escort to the aid delivery sent in 10 trucks clearly marked with the distinctive blue-and-white labels of the WFP.
In Tirana, a bomb destroyed the private car of a former Tirana police chief on Tuesday, but no one was injured, the Albanian news agency ATA said.
The blast completely gutted the small car around 5 a.m. (0300 GMT) in a square in central Tirana and shattered the windows of a nearby restaurant.
The motive for the attack was not known and ATA did not identify the officer.
The World Bank will send a mission to Albania by the end of the month to assess how much money is needed for reconstruction projects, a bank official said.
The mission will examine the damage caused to Albania's infrastructure by weeks of armed unrest, Franco Passacantando, a World Bank executive director, told a conference on Albania in Rome on Monday.
